Meghna is a B.Tech (AI & ML) student at Atria University in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India.

Meghna is a curious builder and explorer who enjoys learning by building things. She's curious about how technology can solve everyday problems, and likes experimenting with new tools, turning ideas into projects, and learning something new along the way.

This portfolio showcases Meghna, a B.Tech (AI & ML) student at Atria University in Bengaluru, Karnataka, who enjoys learning by building things. It features four projects — TasteOrbit, Project Panopticon, Automated Invoice Processing & Anomaly Detection, and Memory of a City — plus a Digital Twin chat widget you can ask about her background and work.

Meghna's projects include TasteOrbit (Restaurant Insights & Quality Prediction), Project Panopticon (Intelligent Exam Proctoring), Automated Invoice Processing & Anomaly Detection, and Memory of a City. Ask about any of them by name for more detail!

data.name: TasteOrbit
data.summary: TasteOrbit: Restaurant Insights & Quality Prediction is a classification model predicting whether Bengaluru restaurants are highly rated, using a Zomato dataset — location, cuisine, cost, and vote count as features.
data.purpose: To predict whether a Bengaluru restaurant will be highly rated.
data.problem: Determining restaurant quality/rating from available data such as location, cuisine, cost, and vote count.
features: Classifies whether a restaurant is highly rated or not
Uses a Zomato dataset with location, cuisine, cost, and vote count as features
Trained with a Logistic Regression model
data.implementation: Uses a Zomato dataset with location, cuisine, cost, and vote count as input features, classified with a Logistic Regression model.
data.outcome: Reaches about 85.7% validation accuracy with Logistic Regression.

data.name: Project Panopticon
data.summary: Project Panopticon: Intelligent Exam Proctoring is a precision-first exam-proctoring pipeline built during an AI internship.
data.purpose: To proctor exams while eliminating false cheating accusations.
data.problem: Reliably detecting cheating in exams without wrongly flagging honest students.
features: Merges asynchronous video and system-event telemetry
Engineers rolling-window features from that telemetry
Raises the decision threshold to 90% confidence to reduce false positives
data.implementation: Merges asynchronous video and system-event telemetry, engineers rolling-window features, and classifies with a Random Forest model using a 90% confidence decision threshold.
data.outcome: Raising the decision threshold to 90% confidence eliminates false cheating accusations.

data.name: Automated Invoice Processing & Anomaly Detection
data.summary: Automated Invoice Processing & Anomaly Detection is an end-to-end pipeline that reads invoice images, extracts fields (invoice number, vendor, amount), then flags suspicious invoices.
data.purpose: To automate reading invoices and detecting anomalous/suspicious ones.
data.problem: Manually processing invoices and spotting anomalies is slow and error-prone.
features: Extracts invoice number, vendor, and amount via OpenCV preprocessing, Tesseract OCR, and regex
Flags suspicious invoices using Z-score and Isolation Forest anomaly detection
data.implementation: Preprocesses invoice images with OpenCV, extracts fields with Tesseract OCR and regex, then flags anomalies using Z-score and Isolation Forest.
data.outcome: Processed 117 invoices at a 94.8% parsing success rate.

data.name: Memory of a City
data.summary: Memory of a City is a Bengaluru-focused urban intelligence site exploring how three neighbourhoods — Indiranagar, Koramangala, and Whitefield — changed between 2010 and 2026.
data.purpose: To explore and explain how three Bengaluru neighbourhoods changed over time.
data.problem: Understanding what might account for urban change in these neighbourhoods, grounded only in the site's prepared dataset.
features: Explores change across three neighbourhoods — Indiranagar, Koramangala, and Whitefield — between 2010 and 2026
Includes an AI "City Change Investigator" that explains what might account for the change
The AI investigator is grounded only in the site's own prepared dataset and never invents facts or statistics
data.implementation: A React/Vite frontend with a Node.js/Express backend; the "City Change Investigator" feature uses the Gemini API, grounded only in the site's own prepared dataset.
